E1.title: Climate
E1.heading: Temperature and humidity
E1.goal: Read an AHT20 over I2C once a second and turn its raw 20-bit words into °C and % humidity, then work out the dew point.
steps: Unplug USB. Wire the AHT20 as in the table: four jumpers, VIN to 3V3.
Run the command. The monitor starts with an I2C scan: you should see 0x38 (AHT20).
Every second a line shows T= and RH=.
Hold the sensor between two fingers: the temperature climbs within a few seconds.
Breathe on it gently: humidity jumps, then settles back.
E1.note: Scan finds nothing? Swap SDA and SCL, check 3V3 and GND. Temperature a few degrees high? The board warms the sensor: move it away on longer wires.

E2.title: Air pressure
E2.heading: Pressure and altitude
E2.goal: Read a BMP280, show air pressure in hPa and turn it into height above sea level with the barometric formula.
steps: Wire the BMP280 as in the table. Its address is 0x76 (or 0x77 if SDO is tied high).
Run the command. Check the scan line, then watch P= and alt=.
Lift the board from the floor to above your head: altitude changes by about 2 m.
Type your local sea-level pressure from a weather site into sea 1009.5 for a true altitude.
E2.note: Altitude drifts during the day: the weather changes the pressure too. Set the sea-level reference again, or use it only for differences.

E3.title: Motion
E3.heading: Tilt with an accelerometer
E3.goal: Read the MPU6050's three accelerometer axes and work out pitch and roll from gravity, like a spirit level.
steps: Wire the MPU6050 as in the table. The scan should show 0x68.
Lay the board flat: az reads about 16384, which is 1 g.
Tilt it forward and back: pitch follows. Tilt it sideways: roll follows.
Shake it: the numbers jump, because the sensor feels your hand as well as gravity.
E3.note: Pitch and roll from the accelerometer are only right when the board is still. For smooth angles while moving, the next step is to blend in the gyroscope.

E4.title: Weather station
E4.heading: All three on one bus, on the screen
E4.goal: Put the AHT20, BMP280 and MPU6050 on the same two I2C wires and show a live weather station on the 1.9″ screen, with a comfort word for the room.

wiring.title: Sensors: all three on the same four wires
head: Sensor pin
ESP32-S3
Role

steps: Keep the screen wired as in lesson 03.
Join the three sensors' VIN, GND, SDA and SCL together (a small breadboard helps), then to the board.
Run the command. The scan must list 0x38, 0x68 and 0x76.
The screen shows temperature, humidity, pressure, tilt and a comfort word.
Warm or breathe on the AHT20 and watch the comfort word change.
E4.note: One sensor missing from the scan? Unplug the others and test it alone: a wrong wire on one board can hold the whole bus down.
